# vint — agent guide

vint is a vanilla TypeScript UI framework: real DOM, no VDOM, no JSX, no build
step. VanJS-shaped tag functions; Solid-faithful reactivity. If you know
Solid's semantics, they apply here exactly wherever the names match. Full
behavioral contract: docs/contract.md (clause numbers cited below).

Import everything from the package root (or `./src/index.ts`):

    import { createSignal, createMemo, createEffect, createResource,
             tags, tagsNS, mount, Show, Switch, Match, For,
             onMount, onCleanup, untrack, batch, on,
             createRoot, createRenderEffect, getOwner, runWithOwner } from "vint"

## The six rules

Almost every mistake with vint violates one of these.

**1. A component runs once. Reactivity lives in function positions.** (R1, R2)
A component is a plain function returning DOM. It never re-runs. A signal read
directly in the component body is a one-shot untracked read; a *function*
child or prop is a live binding.

    const [n, setN] = createSignal(0)
    div(n())            // WRONG — renders 0 forever
    div(n)              // right — live text binding
    div(() => `${n()}s`)                    // right — computed text
    div({ class: () => (n() > 3 ? "hot" : "") })  // right — reactive prop

**2. Exactly one way to read and write.** (R4)
`const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0)`. Read `count()`, write
`setCount(1)` or `setCount(c => c + 1)`. There is no `.val`, no `.value`, no
store, no proxy. Update arrays/objects immutably:

    setTodos(prev => [...prev, todo])            // right
    todos().push(todo)                           // WRONG — invisible to vint (E-FOR-SAMEREF)

**3. `For` for lists, keyed. Never `.map` for dynamic lists.** (C2)
`each` takes a function; object rows need a `key`. Rows keep their DOM across
reorders; removed rows are disposed. `children` runs once per key — reactive
parts inside a row must themselves be function positions.

    For({ each: todos, key: t => t.id,
          children: (item, index) => li(() => item().title) })
    ul(() => todos().map(t => li(t.title)))      // works but rebuilds every row on every change

**4. `Show`/`Switch` branch on booleans; branches are thunks.** (C1, C3)
`Show({ when: n, children: () => div(...) })` rebuilds only when
`Boolean(when())` flips — a value change while truthy does not rebuild, so
render current values with bindings inside the branch, not by closure.
A binding that returns `null` first renders fine later (D3) — placeholder
`display:none` divs are never needed.

**5. Effects for side effects only; memos are pure; cleanups are automatic.**
(R5, R7, O2) `createMemo` for derived values (cached, lazy, equality-gated) —
never write a signal inside one (E-WRITE-IN-MEMO). `createEffect` for side
effects — reads are tracked, re-runs after its dependencies change, and
everything registered with `onCleanup` during a run is disposed before the
next run, so listeners/timers can't duplicate:

    createEffect(() => {
      const t = setInterval(tick, delay())
      onCleanup(() => clearInterval(t))          // runs before every re-run and on unmount
    })

To depend on signals without tracking the body, use `on`:
`createEffect(on([a, b], ([av, bv], prev) => {...}, { defer: true }))` (R11).

**6. Async goes through `createResource`.** (A1–A3)
No hand-rolled loading/error sentinel signals.

    const [user, { refetch, mutate }] = createResource(userId, id => api.fetchUser(id))
    Show({ when: () => user.loading, children: () => Spinner() })
    p(() => user.error ? String(user.error) : "")
    div(() => user()?.name ?? "")

Source accessor `false`/`null`/`undefined` skips fetching. Stale responses are
discarded (last fetch wins). Unlike Solid, `user()` NEVER throws — errors are
only in `user.error` (A3).

## DOM specifics

- `tags.div(propsObject?, ...children)`. Custom elements are ordinary tags:
  `tags["vi-button"]({ label: "Save" })`. SVG:
  `const svg = tagsNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg")`.
- Props route to a settable property when one exists, else an attribute (D6).
  Force with `"prop:x"` / `"attr:x"`. `true` → empty attribute, `false`/null →
  removed. `style` takes a string or a camelCase object.
- Events: `onclick: fn` (lowercased name), `"on:vi-change": fn` (exact name).
  Attached once, never reactive — branch inside the handler (D8).
- No `ref`: the tag call returns the element. `const el = div(...); el.focus()`.
- `mount(container, App)` once per app; it returns a disposer that removes the
  DOM and every subscription (D9).
- `onMount(fn)` runs once after the component's DOM bindings settle,
  synchronously; its return value is ignored — use `onCleanup` (O4).

## Guarantees you can rely on

- No stale reads: memos are glitch-free; effects always see settled memos (R6).
- Writes during effects cascade in the same flush; nothing is dropped (R8).
- One throwing effect never blocks others; the error rethrows after the flush
  (R10). `batch(fn)` coalesces multiple writes into one flush (R9).
- Disposal is total: after unmount, writes touch nothing, listeners are gone,
  no leaks (O5).

## Errors are prompts

Dev-mode errors name the fix — do what they say. Codes: E-LOOP (effect feeds
itself — untrack the write), E-WRITE-IN-MEMO (move the write to an effect),
E-CIRCULAR-MEMO, E-DISPOSED-MEMO (lift the memo to a longer-lived owner),
E-NO-OWNER (create it under mount/createRoot), E-FOR-ARRAY (wrap: `each: () =>
items`), E-FOR-DUPKEY (make keys unique), E-FOR-SAMEREF (update immutably).

## Reference example

examples/todo.ts is the canonical app shape: signals + memos at the top,
event handlers writing immutably, `Show` + keyed `For` for the list,
one `mount` at the end. examples/fetch.ts is the canonical resource usage.
